title: The Contract Test for a Hardware Interface: Eleven Promises Every Drive Must Keep, Checked on a Fake, a Simulator and a Board Alike

questions.question: What does an interface not say?
options: What happens when they are called
How many functions it has
What types the functions take
Which class implements it
questions.explanation: The signatures say what can be called. What a stop must do, or what a command that is not a number must do, is written nowhere in them.

questions.question: How many promises did the fake of 22-01 break once fixed?
options: 1, the watchdog
2, the watchdog and the NaN
questions.explanation: Before the fix the clamp as first written broke two. Fixed, the fake kept all eleven.

questions.question: What did std::min(limit, NaN) return?
options: The limit, so a NaN became full speed
NaN, which stopped the base
Zero
The smaller of the two
questions.explanation: std::min returns its first argument unless the second is less, and nothing compares less with a NaN. So a command that was not a number became the limit.

questions.question: Why does the contract make a fresh drive for each promise?
options: A drive cannot be used twice
To test the constructor
Fresh drives run faster
So one promise's state cannot hide or cause another's failure
questions.explanation: A drive left moving by one check could fail or pass the next for the wrong reason. Starting each from rest keeps them apart.

questions.question: Why test the contract with broken drives as well as good ones?
options: Broken drives are easier to write
To show that it can fail: a test that has never been seen to fail proves little
To measure how fast the contract runs
To find bugs in the broken drives
questions.explanation: Each of six drives with one fault was caught by the promise it breaks. That is the evidence that the promises check something.

questions.question: What is the use of passing the expected limits to the contract?
options: It lets the contract skip promises
It makes the contract run faster
The same function can judge a toy base and a heavy one
It tells the drive what to do
questions.explanation: The promises are the same for every drive. What differs is how fast it may go and how long a stop may take, and those are handed in.
